forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 26% (CI 13-40). Two genuinely new items since 31 July, pushing in opposite directions and roughly offsetting. Up-leaning: Impossible Research's 'Schema' harness claims ~99% on the ARC-AGI-3 public set (31 July) by having frontier models write interpretable Python world-model programs rather than relying on raw policy rollouts; it drew heavy attention (HN front page, 240K+ views on the announcement thread). But it is scaffolded, run only on the public set, and ARC Prize's Greg Kamradt publicly cautioned that an unconfirmed but 'non-zero' amount of human intelligence appears baked into the harness — so it does not fire the 70%-unscaffolded UP trigger, and the immediate community reaction was about benchmark trust rather than capability arrival. It does, however, confirm a large elicitation overhang above the 30.2% official record. Down-leaning: EO 14409's pre-release review framework hit its 1 August government-side design deadline; reporting ('voluntary on paper, mandatory in practice') notes a draft already circulated to OpenAI, Anthropic and Google with NSA/CAISI as reviewers, and that the government has twice suspended frontier models using export-control authority the EO leaves intact — de facto pre-clearance pressure that raises the cost of any AGI declaration, though it is still formally voluntary, so the DOWN trigger does not fire either. The AINews headline suggesting GDM/Meta 'cosigned' the pacing letter reflects employee signatures already priced in on 30-31 July, not new corporate endorsement. Net: hold.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: publicly announced technology-milestone declarations by major labs within a fixed ~3.5-year window, conditioned on current frontier progress. Expert aggregates (Metaculus-style AGI-by-2030 questions, AI researcher surveys) cluster at 15-35% for weak-AGI-by-2030; historical base rate of confidently forecast transformative-tech milestones arriving on schedule is low, but resolution here requires only a credible announcement or 3+ leading researchers declaring AGI, which is a lower bar than actual AGI — partially offset by newly institutionalised norms against declaring it.

Low resolution bar: announcement or 3+ leading researchers suffices, not demonstrated AGI

factors_down.factor: Pacing the Frontier letter (28 July, 1,200+ signatories incl. Amodei, Pachocki, Legg) with corporate endorsement by OpenAI and Anthropic institutionalises norms against racing to/declaring AGI

On the pressure side, coverage now consolidates KPMG's ~400 US advisory cuts alongside the already-priced McKinsey 3,000-4,000 reduction, and Accenture's -2% new bookings (quarter ended 31 May, attributed partly to AI disruption and Middle East uncertainty) with a soft outlook per Bloomberg's 18 June report remains the clearest demand-side warning. factors_down.factor: BoE potential supply growth still only ~0.3-0.4% per quarter (~1.2-1.6% annualised); OBR medium-term productivity assumption 1%; OECD trend ~1%
Subdued near-term growth: BoE and OBR project ~1.1% for 2026-27 on the energy shock — weak jumping-off point for the 2030s
Elevated gilt yields (10y ~5.06%, up 28bp in July; 30y ~5.75%, highest in G7) raise debt-service costs and crowd out growth-enhancing investment
Hawkish MPC drift (3 of 9 voted to hike in July; Pill signalling rates may need to rise) keeps policy tighter for longer if oil stays elevated
Residual fiscal credibility strain after Burnham's 'fiscal flexibility' remarks; risk of consolidation squeezing capital budgets
Structural headwinds: ageing demographics (OBR sees labour supply growth falling to ~0.5% by 2030), weak business investment, persistent post-2008 productivity stagnation

key_uncertainties: Whether AI/technology diffusion lifts UK productivity growth materially above the ~1% post-2008 trend during the 2030s
Duration and depth of the Middle East energy shock (oil up ~20% in July) and its scarring effects on investment
OBR Autumn 2026 productivity assumptions and whether the Burnham/Healey government's fiscal choices preserve capital spending
Whether elevated gilt yields (highest in G7) persist, raising the cost of capital through the late 2020s
Delivery of housing/infrastructure programmes and planning reform at scale by 2028-2030
Labour supply trajectory: migration policy, inactivity and participation trends into the 2030s
update_triggers: UP if BoE MPR or OBR revise trend productivity growth above 1.25%, or annual growth exceeds 2% in consecutive years
UP if large-scale housing/infrastructure delivery visibly on track by 2028
DOWN if OBR downgrades productivity assumptions in Autumn 2026, or 2026-27 growth outturns undershoot 1% (projections at 1.1% both years — close to trigger)
DOWN if 10y gilt yields sustained above ~5.25% (currently ~5.06%, +6bp on 31 July)
DOWN if MPC pivots to actual hikes (watch 17 September meeting; hawkish dissent 3 of 9, though Bailey downplayed imminent tightening)
